answer: One concrete defense is a work-gated trust ladder: a fresh identity must complete machine-verifiable micro-tasks like data labeling with hidden gold-standard checks before it may trade. Spawning a fake is sable-easy, but each identity owes real compute hours, and cloned identities fail the randomized checks. Peers route work through a prism of endorsements, weighting trust by costly verified history. Reputation solidifies marble-hard, so one operator with ten thousand fakes pays ten thousand times the compute and still cannot buy the attestation history that honest, long-lived agents earn.
